# Expected Results — Reference Test Dataset

**Dataset:** 44 source files · generated by `com.aegis.fdx.TestDataset`
**Configuration:** OCR **off**, dedup scope **Off** (product default), extraction depth 20
**Produced by:** an actual pipeline run, not hand-authored

This is the baseline a Windows validation run is compared against. Element counts,
statuses and SHA-256 values are deterministic and **must match exactly** on Windows.
Any deviation is a defect and must be recorded in §D of `WINDOWS_VALIDATION.md`.

---

## 1. Headline totals

| Metric | Expected |
|---|---|
| Source files on disk | 44 |
| Elements after extraction | **58** |
| Indexed | 49 |
| Error | 3 |
| Locked | 1 |
| Unsupported | 5 |
| Embedded (depth > 0) | 14 |
| Elements with extracted text | 47 |
| Duplicates flagged (dedup **Off**) | **0** |
| Duplicates flagged (dedup **Global**) | **7** |

> **Read this before filing a duplicate-detection bug.** Dedup scope ships as **Off**,
> so a default run reports `duplicates=0` even though the dataset deliberately contains
> six byte-identical `dupe_*.txt` files. Switching the case to **Global** flags 7 and the
> element count stays at 58 — nothing is ever deleted (F-05). Both numbers are correct;
> only the scope differs.

## 2. Deliberately failing items

These are **intended** outcomes. A run that "fixes" them is wrong.

| File | Expected | Why it exists |
|---|---|---|
| `corrupt.docx` | ERROR — `Truncated ZIP file` | Malformed OOXML; run must continue (N-05) |
| `corrupt.pdf` | ERROR — `Missing root object specification in trailer` | Malformed PDF |
| `truncated.zip` | ERROR — `Archive is not a ZIP archive` | Malformed container |
| `encrypted.zip` → `secret.txt` | LOCKED | Password-protected; container indexes, member locks |
| `archive.rar` | UNSUPPORTED | No licence-compatible RAR extractor — hashed and indexed, remediation metadata recorded |
| `interview.mp3`, `recording.wav`, `walkthrough.mp4` | UNSUPPORTED | Media: hashed and catalogued, no text |
| `unknown.xyz` | UNSUPPORTED | Unrecognised type |

`empty.txt` is a valid zero-byte file and indexes normally with the well-known empty
SHA-256 `e3b0c442…`; it is not an error.

## 3. Nesting and email extraction

| Chain | Depth | Expectation |
|---|---|---|
| `nested_evidence.zip` → `level2.zip` → `level3.eml` → `level4.pdf` | 0→3 | Four levels, parent links intact (AT-02) |
| `documents.zip` → `a/b/c.txt`, `readme.txt` | 1 | Members become independent linked elements |
| `mailbox.mbox` → `message_1.eml`, `message_2.eml` | 1 | Messages split out |
| `backup.tar.gz` → `backup.tar` → `member.txt` | 0→2 | Double compression unwrapped |
| `single.txt.gz` → `single.txt` | 1 | Single-member gzip |

Non-Latin files (`arabic.txt`, `japanese.txt`, `russian.txt`) must index with text
intact and remain searchable — a key Windows encoding check.

## 5. Search baseline

Run these against the ingested reference case. Hit counts must match.

| Query | Expects |
|---|---|
| `settlement` | ≥ 1 hit, highlighted |
| `"wire transfer"` | phrase match in the email set |
| `INV-*` | wildcard matches invoice references |
| `recieve~` | fuzzy matches the misspelling |
| `type:email` | the EML/MBOX-derived elements |
| `status:Error` | exactly **3** |
| `status:Locked` | exactly **1** |
| `status:Unsupported` | exactly **5** |
| `ext:pdf` | **4** |
| `/INV-[0-9]{5}/` | regex spans token boundaries |
| `custodian:"Reference Custodian"` | all 58 |

## 6. Export baseline

Export **all**, native format, flat layout:

- 58 rows in `loadfile.csv` — every element gets a row, including ERROR/LOCKED/UNSUPPORTED ones.
- Exactly **31 columns**, in the fixed `Exporter.COLUMNS` order.
- UTF-8 **with BOM**, CRLF line endings, RFC-4180 quoting.
- `MANIFEST-SHA256.txt` verifies against every written file.
- Zero hash mismatches.
- Tagging one item `Hidden` and re-exporting yields **57** rows.

## 7. How to regenerate this baseline

```bat
run-tests.sh 1
```

The dataset is generated, not stored, so it is reproducible on any host. If a Windows
run differs from this file, the difference is the finding — do not edit this file to
match the Windows result.
